newsitem.title: JORDAN: Israeli foreign minister meets Jordanian PM.
newsitem.headline: Israeli foreign minister meets Jordanian PM.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy held talks with Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti on Thursday.
Levy did not speak to reporters as he left Kabariti's officie for talks with King Hussein.
Kabariti, who on Wednesday warned Israel that its encouragement of Jewish settlements on occupied Arab land threatened to torpedo Israeli-Palestinian talks, told reporters:
"(Settlements) are an illegal issue which contradict the principle of land for peace...and they are a direct threat to the overall peace process."

Jordan signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994, but relations between the two countries were strained by Israel's decision in September to open a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem, sparking widespread violence in which at least 75 people were killed.

Levy will also inaugurate a new Israeli embassy building in Amman during his visit. Israeli diplomats have been operating from offices in a five-star hotel since they opened their mission to Jordan in December 1994.
